P1.evidence: Setter notes were used well and repeatedly — the age, and the fact that Kim had already pre-framed the cost ('I already heard from Kim that he already gave you an insight from what the costs are going to look like'), which is the check doing exactly what it is for. Everything else in the phase collapsed. The prospect talked for the first two and a half minutes unprompted and the rep never reset. No four-part frame, only a fragment ('first of all, it's important to see if it's actually going to be a good fit'), no frame agreement asked, and the open question never posed. Instead the rep's first real move at 00:02:44 was a commitment question — 'do you want to make the commitment for yourself to doing three to four times a week, 30 to 45 minute workouts?' — which is a Phase 6 move asked in minute three, before any baseline at all.

P2.evidence: Six of nine ran properly. Weight, height and age were all asked. Work was established richly — school counsellor, football and basketball official, track coach, further certification, officiating season. Training was asked and produced the rowing machine, bike, Planet Fitness membership and the apartment gym. Diet was asked, then pushed on twice ('what's horrible?' and whether processed food was daily or weekly). The injury probe was the strongest in the batch: severity on a 1-10 scale plus the origin question, 'is it something that has been around for a long time?', which uncovered that the lower back came from lifting his disabled wife into a wheelchair. But P2c is a serious miss. Health conditions were never asked, and the prospect twice volunteered that he is a 25-year diabetic with possible kidney involvement, and twice got no response of any kind. Sleep and energy were also never asked of a 69-year-old.

P3.evidence: Strong. The physique question was open and specific and produced a measurable target (waist 40-42 down to 35-36). The bridge landed hard — 'why is it so important for you to stay so healthy? Why don't you just say, I'm in good state, I'll leave the health on the side now?' — and produced the real driver: 'I just don't want to be a statistic. The average age is 64, I already exceeded that. The next stage I may encounter issues is 78... I want to get to 78 standing and walking.' Future-pacing ran and drew the most human answer in the batch: asked how it would feel to reach that goal still moving well, he said 'I would be married, hopefully.' The reflect-back was accurate and confirmed. Only P3f is missing, and it was available — students, young athletes he wants to teach, and declining friends were all on the table and nobody asked who else this affects.

P4.evidence: The root cause was found quickly and cleanly. The rep caught an offhand remark and probed it — 'I just want to clarify one thing you said, like free weights, you can't be consistent with that, is that because you have to go to a gym with that?' — and the prospect named the gap himself: 'it's just getting to those spaces' and 'I've always done exercise in my immediate space, and I get the results that I want because it's consistent.' That is P4c, P4d and P4e in one exchange. What was never asked is P4f, and this is the call where it mattered most: the prospect is a certified track coach with USATF credentials who says outright 'I have certifications to do all that kind of stuff'. For a man who already has the information, 'why can't you stick to it on your own' is the whole sale, and it went unasked — which is also why he ended up buying a self-study course.

P5.evidence: The settle question ran in inverted form and worked, and the why-not follow-up was effectively the same question that produced the statistics answer. But the cost of inaction was supplied almost entirely by the prospect, not built by the rep — the friends in their 80s with their legs gone, the same-age friend in intensive care after a stroke, the actuarial numbers. The rep's contribution was 'it doesn't sound like you're willing to settle for that either', an assertion rather than a question. No two-year picture was drawn, and no line in the sand was requested; the commitment was asserted ('it sounds like you're committed, it sounds like you're ready to go') and merely agreed to.

P6.evidence: Clean. The belief check ran — 'when it comes to the coaching itself, you feel like, yes, this is going to help me get better?' answered 'it's going to help me, yes.' The go-all-in question ran and produced a precise answer: 'do you feel like there's anything that would stop you from getting to the goals?' / 'The only thing that's going to stop me is what's going to cost me.' The rep then isolated correctly — 'outside of cost, because of course it's always a factor, but outside of cost' — and got 'that's about it right now'. Price was withheld until after that yes.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and payment was pursued three separate times, correctly, but nothing was collected and no link was sent, so step one is incomplete. The rep did describe the mechanics of what would happen on Friday — 'we do a payment, $200 a month, you get an agreement and also directly comes the link to join the whole self-study part' — but describing the steps is not running them. Steps 2 to 4 are genuinely not applicable: the self-study tier has no Trevor onboarding call. The weak point is the follow-up itself, left as 'let's stay in contact' with no fixed time and the rep travelling to Germany that day.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger at 00:40:07, 'the only thing that's going to stop me is what's going to cost me'. Good moves ran: the isolation, cash available now ('what do you have available now?' — 'nothing, zero'), the leftover-after-bills question ('is it after bills are paid, you seriously have basically zero at the end of the month?'), and a probe on the one credit card with $400 available including whether emergencies actually happen. Missing: the number of cards and total available credit, even though he volunteered 'I have others' with outstanding balances; the 'are you comfortable having an open, honest conversation about exactly where you're at financially' preamble; the 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' reframe; and above all investments. This man has multiple pensions and a six-figure income and was never asked about savings, retirement accounts or assets. The rep took him at his word that zero meant zero.

A clean not-the-right-time with a specific date attached: 'I'll be willing to do the $1,200 a month, but I have to wait until September', because his Social Security increase lands when he turns 70. The rep resisted once — 'we don't want to wait per se until September' — and then solved it structurally with the self-study bridge, which is a legitimate and arguably better answer than the script. But none of the OD moves ran. 'The longer you wait the harder this gets' had an unusually literal form available here: a 69-year-old diabetic with declining annual strength, whose same-age friend was in intensive care that week. That argument was sitting in the transcript in the prospect's own words and was never made.

The most serious script gap in the batch: an undisclosed-risk chronic condition, volunteered twice and acknowledged zero times. 'I also may be having some issues with my kidneys because I'm diabetic' and 'I've been diabetic for 25 years'. The playbook has no health-screening step and no clearance protocol, so nothing prompted the rep to react, and he did not — he went on to sell a calorie-deficit protocol with restricted eating windows, which for a 25-year diabetic is a medication-timing and glycaemic-control question, not a preference. Same clinical blind spot already logged from the Tyron Giuliani call and repeated here with the Scott Hamilton AFib disclosure in this same batch. The ICP has no clinical criterion and neither does the script.

Second gap: a dated future income event. This is not 'I can't afford it' and not 'now is bad' — it is 'I will have the money on a known date and not before'. OC assumes there is money to find and OD assumes the timing objection is a dodge; neither is true here. The rep improvised well, bridging with a lower tier creditable against the full price, which kept the relationship alive and got a start date. Worth scripting properly, since the same shape will recur with anyone on a pay cycle, a bonus, a tax refund or a pension uplift.
No think-about-it. He gave a specific reason and a specific date rather than a deferral, and volunteered 'I want to do this'.
Widower living alone, and explicit that no one else is involved: 'I'm here by myself, I live peacefully, mind my business, I do what I have to do, and I don't have to explain nothing to nobody.'
No fear or doubt about the method or his ability. He is a certified coach who understands training adaptation and said so at length.

notes: Phases 3 and 6 ran well and the pricing was, for once, quoted honestly and consistently — three payments of $2,000 or six of $1,200 with the rep saying outright that instalments cost more. Two things to act on. First and urgently: this man volunteered that he is a 25-year diabetic with possible kidney involvement, twice, and got no acknowledgement either time, then had a calorie-deficit eating-window protocol sold to him. That needs a screening step in the script, not a coaching note. Second: he is a certified track coach who already has the information, and P4f — 'the information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' — was never asked, which is both the missing sale and the reason he defaulted to a self-study product. Also fix the follow-up discipline: a verbal yes with no link sent, no payment taken and no fixed call time is not a close, it is a hope.
